name: manual_516ced
claim: A caller-supplied ceiling (e.g. explicit_cap_microusd on a budget-reservation call) must be independently bounded by the actual remaining resource, not just validated against the caller's own worst_case value. Validating 'worst_case <= explicit_cap' alone lets a caller bypass the real limit by simply passing an inflated cap -- the fix is to also clamp the effective cap to whatever is genuinely left ('if policy_cap > remaining: policy_cap = remaining') before checking worst_case against it. This is a general pattern for any two-tier limit system (a caller-declared ceiling plus a system-wide remaining pool), not specific to this one ledger.
conditions: explicit cap bound remaining budget bypass validation two-tier limit resource reservation pattern

decisions.notes: 2026-08-21, PT PR #359, orchestrator/tier5_budget.py reserve(), caught by CodeRabbit review #4983381866 and confirmed as a real bug (not just style) via a new test: reserve 9_500_000 of a 10_000_000 daily limit, leaving 500_000 remaining, then a second call with worst_case=600_000 and explicit_cap_microusd=5_000_000 would have succeeded pre-fix despite only 500_000 actually being left.

rationale: 2026-08-21, PT PR #359, orchestrator/tier5_budget.py reserve(), caught by CodeRabbit review #4983381866 and confirmed as a real bug (not just style) via a new test: reserve 9_500_000 of a 10_000_000 daily limit, leaving 500_000 remaining, then a second call with worst_case=600_000 and explicit_cap_microusd=5_000_000 would have succeeded pre-fix despite only 500_000 actually being left.
